warmup.description: Activate the scapular stabilizers and prime the shoulder girdle before loading.
movements: Thoracic rotation in half-kneeling — 8 reps each side

main_exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Overhead Press
main_exercises.load_guidance: Choose a weight where rep 11 feels genuinely challenging but form stays clean — roughly 7/10 effort.
main_exercises.form_cue: Press the dumbbells slightly in front of your forehead, not directly overhead, to keep the shoulder joint in a safe position.

main_exercises.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
main_exercises.load_guidance: Drive your elbows back until you feel a full lat contraction — use a load you could do 14 reps with if you had to.
main_exercises.form_cue: Keep your chest pinned to the bench and avoid shrugging your shoulders at the top of the pull.

main_exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Chest Press
main_exercises.load_guidance: Moderate effort — leave 2-3 reps in reserve on every set, prioritizing a controlled 2-second lowering phase.
main_exercises.form_cue: Lower the dumbbells to the outside of your chest with elbows at roughly a 45-degree angle to your torso.

main_exercises.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row (elbow on bench)
main_exercises.load_guidance: Match or slightly exceed the load from the chest-supported row — unilateral work lets you focus each side independently.
main_exercises.form_cue: Row the dumbbell toward your hip, not your armpit, to maximize lat engagement over bicep.

main_exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
main_exercises.load_guidance: Light load — you should be able to hold the top position for one count on every rep. Ego weight kills the stimulus here.
main_exercises.form_cue: Lead with your pinkies slightly higher than your thumbs and stop at shoulder height, not above.

main_exercises.name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl
main_exercises.load_guidance: Pick a weight where the last 3 reps require genuine focus but your shoulder stays still and your elbow stays tucked.
main_exercises.form_cue: Keep your wrist neutral throughout — the hammer grip targets the brachialis and forearm, so resist any urge to supinate.

cooldown.description: Lengthen the chest, lats, and shoulders after loading and bring the nervous system down.
movements: Doorway chest stretch — 45 seconds each side
Cross-body shoulder stretch — 30 seconds each side
Child's pose with arms extended — 60 seconds
Supine thoracic extension over a rolled mat or foam roller — 60 seconds

phase_notes.menstrual: If energy and discomfort allow, this session is manageable at reduced output — drop load by 10-15% and prioritize form over challenge. Skip if cramping is significant and opt for rest instead.
phase_notes.follicular: Rising estrogen supports strength adaptation well here — this is a good phase to push toward the top of each rep range and note your loads for future reference.
phase_notes.ovulatory: Peak power output makes this an ideal session to feel strong and coordinated; you may find the prescribed loads feel lighter than usual, which is normal and worth noting.
phase_notes.early_luteal: Progesterone is rising but performance typically remains solid in early luteal — complete the session as written, staying honest about effort without pushing into late-set grinding.
phase_notes.late_luteal: Fatigue and mood shifts may make the session feel harder than the numbers suggest — reduce rest periods only if energy is genuinely high, and treat leaving 3 reps in reserve as the goal rather than 2.
